title: Chemical Equilibrium and Le Chatelier's Principle
seo_title: Year 12 Chemistry: Chemical Equilibrium Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium in closed systems; Le Chatelier's principle for changes in concentration, pressure and temperature; equilibrium constants and the reaction quotient; calculations with K; equilibrium in industry and in natural systems. (Senior Secondary Chemistry, Unit 3: Equilibrium, acids and redox reactions)
meta_desc: Free Year 12 Chemistry worksheets on chemical equilibrium: dynamic equilibrium, Le Chatelier's principle, equilibrium expressions, calculating K, the reaction quotient and the Haber process. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Only temperature changes the value of K.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a closed system a reversible reaction reaches dynamic equilibrium: forward and reverse rates are equal and concentrations stay constant. Le Chatelier's principle: a change in concentration, pressure or temperature shifts the equilibrium to partly oppose it. A catalyst only makes equilibrium come faster.

For aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD, K = [C]ᶜ[D]ᵈ ÷ [A]ᵃ[B]ᵇ. Compare the reaction quotient Q with K to predict the direction. For an exothermic forward reaction, raising the temperature lowers K.

Example

H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI: [H₂] = [I₂] = 0.10, [HI] = 0.70 mol/L. K?

K = 0.70² ÷ (0.10 × 0.10)

Answer: 49

Example

Q = 20, K = 49. Which way does the reaction go?

Q < K

more products needed

Answer: forward (to the right)

Common mistakes

  • Saying the concentrations of reactants and products are equal at equilibrium.
  • Thinking a catalyst shifts the equilibrium.
  • Putting solids or water in the K expression.

faq.q: Why is the Haber process a compromise?
faq.a: Low temperature gives a higher yield of ammonia but a slow rate; about 450 °C, high pressure and an iron catalyst give a good yield quickly enough.

faq.q: Does changing the concentration change K?
faq.a: No. The position of equilibrium shifts, but K changes only with temperature.

items.q: Why must a system be closed to reach equilibrium?
c: no reactants or products can enter or leave
so a catalyst can be added
so the reaction goes to completion
items.e: Open systems cannot reach equilibrium.

items.q: If the concentration of a reactant is increased, which way does the equilibrium shift?
c: to the right, to use up some of the added reactant
items.e: K stays the same.

items.q: An engineer wants more NO from a hot car engine: N<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2NO, the energy change = +181 kJ. Which single change increases the amount of NO at equilibrium?
c: The pressure is decreased (the container is made larger).
The pressure is increased (the container is made smaller).
items.e: the energy change = +181 kJ, so the forward reaction is endothermic. Heating favors the endothermic direction.

items.q: In blood, CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻. What happens to blood pH if a person breathes too fast and loses CO₂?
c: pH rises, because the equilibria shift left and [H⁺] falls
items.e: This is respiratory alkalosis.

The pressure is decreased (the container is made larger).
items.e: the energy change = −9 kJ, so the forward reaction is exothermic. Cooling favors the exothermic direction.
